title: Section 10 ICA — What agreements are contracts

content.overview: All agreements are contracts if made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void. Section 10 is the enforceability gate.

sections.heading: Elements
sections.body: 1. Agreement (offer + acceptance). 2. Free consent (ss. 13–22). 3. Competency (ss. 11–12). 4. Lawful consideration and object (ss. 23–25). 5. Not expressly declared void.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Map facts onto section 10. If consent is vitiated, go to ss. 15–19A (voidable). If object is unlawful, s. 23 (void). If consideration is absent without statutory exception, s. 25.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Civil suit for specific performance (SRA 1963, post-2018 regime subject to ss. 11, 14, 16) or damages (ss. 73–74 ICA). Plead formation facts and any alleged defect. Limitation typically three years under the Limitation Act, 1963 (check the precise article).

illustrations: Two competent adults freely agree to sell a lawful item for a lawful price; section 10 provides the starting test for whether the agreement is a contract.
